There is a confusion in the context snippets due to how they are pasted together.
Snippet 1 mentions Brett Proved (likely a typo for Brett or referring to a different person? Or maybe "Brett Proved" is the subject). Then it lists stats: "Brewers career leader in runs (1,632), hits (3,142) ... Holds AL career record with 123 sacrifice flies."
Snippet 5 explicitly says: "Yount ... finished with 3,142 hits ... He also holds the AL record for career sacrifice flies (123)."
Snippet 6 explicitly says: "George Brett ... Ranks 15th on career hits list with 3,142 ... Holds AL career record with 123 sacrifice flies".
Actually, in real baseball history, George Brett holds the record for hits (3,142) and sacrifice flies (123). Robin Yount also holds the record for sacrifice flies (123) and has 3,142 hits. The context seems to be mixing them or presenting them in parallel.
However, the question asks about "his 20-year career with the Brewers".
George Brett played for the Kansas City Royals (1973-1993) and the Oakland Athletics (1994-1998). He did NOT play for the Brewers.
Robin Yount played for the Milwaukee Brewers from 1974 to 1993 (20 seasons).
Therefore, despite the context snippet potentially attributing the stats to Brett in one place due to poor formatting or shared parentheticals, the only player who fits the description "20-year career with the Brewers" AND has the stats of 3,142 hits and 123 sacrifice flies is Robin Yount. The snippet from the Journal-Times clearly links Yount to the 3,142 hits and the 123 sacrifice flies. The snippet from Asbury Park links Brett to the stats but incorrectly implies he spent all years with the Brewers or uses the stats in a way that conflicts with his actual team history (he was with the Royals). The prompt specifies "During his 20-year career with the Brewers". This is the key discriminator. Only Yount fits the "20-year career with the Brewers" description.
